To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amino‐terminal part of the LexA polypeptide chain contains a DNA‐binding site, and that the DNA‐binding site in the carboxy terminus of the protein is responsible for operator specificity.

(i) The purified amino‐terminal fragment of LexA repressors induces a very similar, if not identical, conformational change in the DNA as the entire repressors, as evidenced by c.d. experiments; (ii) the amino‐terminal fragment binds to the LexA operator with a specificity similar to that of the entire repressor as evidenced by dimethylsulphate methylation experiments.
the amino‐terminal half of the LexA‐repressor binds to DNA in a specific and sequence‐dependent manner, and that the DNA binding domain is located in the amino‐terminal part of the LexA polypeptide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question as to whether the amino‐terminal part of the LexA polypeptide is sufficient to account for DNA binding of the repressor.
the involvement of the carboxy terminus of LexA in DNA binding, whereas the amino terminus is involved in DNA recognition.
the question of whether the amino‐terminal region of LexA repressors is involved in DNA recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino‐terminal part of LexA is involved in specific DNA recognition, but the exact mode of interaction remains to be established.
the amino‐terminal region of the LexA‐like repressor is involved in specific recognition of the operator DNA.
the amino‐terminal region of LexA contains the specific DNA binding site, while the carboxy terminus of the protein is responsible for the oligomerization of the repressor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the amino‐terminal half of the LexA molecule, which is the only part of the repressor that has been sequenced, is sufficient to bind specifically to the recA operator and is also capable of inducing a conformational change in the DNA lattice.
the amino‐terminal region of LexA is a DNA‐binding domain which is responsible for the specific interaction of the repressor with the operator of the RecA gene.

the amino‐terminal part of LexA is involved in the recognition of the operator DNA, and that the conformational changes of the LexA operator complex are induced by the amino‐terminal region of the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LexA binds to DNA via its amino‐terminal domain, which is the first time that a specific DNA binding domain has been identified in the LexA protein.
the amino‐terminal region of LexA is sufficient to bind to the operator and that the carboxy terminus is not required for this interaction.
the amino‐terminal half of LexA repressors binds DNA in vitro with the same efficiency as the entire protein.
